thread.title: MedMen Has The Makings Of Greatness And Could Blaze Above All - Medmen Enterprises Inc. (OTCMKTS:MMNFF) | Seeking Alpha

author: Easterly Winds
title: MedMen Has The Makings Of Greatness And Could Blaze Above All - Medmen Enterprises Inc. (OTCMKTS:MMNFF) | Seeking Alpha
text:
Greatness is a word with immense implications for whoever it is or is not attached to. Defined as a "state of superiority affecting a person" and a "position of power, success, or respect," it is a very strong descriptor. Hence, it has to be robustly justified in the rare instance it is used, lest its value diminishes.
MedMen ( OTCQB:MMNFF ) has the making of greatness as its executive team intends to conquer the high-end of the US cannabis market. Crucially, the intersection of their unique retail rollout strategy with their creation of a mainstream cannabis brand lends credence to their makings of greatness. And, while most of the analyst commentary surrounding the stock has focused on the outsized loss for the fiscal year 2018, the large upcoming lease payments, and the company's seemingly baffling marketing strategy, they have all skipped over the fundamental trajectory established by the company.
Unjustifiably, there is a lot of hype and euphoria surrounding companies in the cannabis space, and I recognize that the title of this article does little to stem this. However, and unlike the muted level of analysis surrounding the space, I will put forward an empirical argument for why MedMen has the makings of greatness and could become one the largest cannabis companies in North America.
Billboard advert for MedMen in California
Relax, It's Legal MedMen's marketing strategy, like everything this company does, has been controversial. A vocal critic described the company's marketing spend as a "pretty dumb way to spend money" as well as "crazy". This myopic way of thinking fails to realize that there are now hundreds if not thousands of cannabis companies in North America as everyone from your Uber driver and your neighbor Dave can get enough capital to launch their dreams of cannabis wealth. It is in such nascent stages that brands are built. As this space matures, we will likely see a large wave of consolidation and bankruptcies. Hence, companies with no brand-led economic moat will likely witness the wholesale destruction of shareholder capital. MedMen's marketing spend is integral for the cultivation of a mainstream cannabis brand which will accrue significant value as the industry matures. Hence, while it's a drag on current earnings in an industry at its dawn, when the sun has set, what would be left is a company positioned firmly at the forefront of the luxury cannabis shopping experience.
The facet has rendered the company less attractive on apple to apple comparisons with its US and Canadian peers. Indeed, the company has its own 25-person in-house agency which runs brand content and retail strategy, SEO practices, search marketing, influencer outreach, and social engagement.
Source: MedMen MD+A for the three and twelve months ended June 30
And the evidence that this is working is becoming more apparent. So, while other analysts focused on the large headline loss for the financial year 2018 and the first quarter of 2019, they fundamentally failed to analyze MedMen's increasingly inherent competitive advantage.
MedMen Is Building The 'MedMen' Of Cannabis MedMen has been called everything from the Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL ) of the cannabis industry to its Starbucks (NASDAQ: SBUX ), Barneys, Target (NYSE: TGT ), and Whole Foods. In fact, if you took a straight vodka shot every time MedMen is compared to a large US retail company, you would run through enough bottles to supply the freshman intake of any mid-sized US college.
But it is not just about fancy stores. With the right design team, any other company could achieve that. It's about a holistic strategy that combines acute branding, with strong retail locations and an impressive shopping experience for customers. This drove an 84.4% conversion rate to overall check-in traffic during the fourth quarter of 2018. It also meant annualized per square foot revenue was $6,257, higher than most companies in the US retail industry.
The signs that MedMen's holistic strategy is paying off are beginning to show.
For the quarter ending September 30, 2018, California realized total retail sales of $349.3 million . Over the same period, MedMen saw its Californian stores generate revenue of $18.5 million, 5.3% of the aggregate sales in California. To put this in context, there are 456 licensed retailers in the state. MedMen also does not yet have any stores in Northern California. According to MedMen, by averaging out every retailer, each would hold 1.8% market share. Hence, with MedMen's 11 stores in the state at the end of the quarter, the company's stores are generating three times more revenue than their competitors.
Again, it is not just about incredibly swanky stores with iPads, MedMen has gained first mover advantage in the creation of an upmarket brand for cannabis retailing. The company also recently moved to hire Michael W. Kramer as its new CFO. This adds a depth to their executive team, as Kramer has three decades of experience including serving as CFO of Apple Retail from 2000 to 2005.
MedMen's forget stoner campaign
Shaping Up To Be A Behemoth Of An Industry At Its Dawn MedMen currently sports the fastest revenue growth rate of any public listed cannabis company in North America, and by extension, the world.
Q3 2018 Q4 2018 Q1 2019 Revenue $7,220,000 $20,568,000 $21,460,000 YoY rev. percentage growth - 1317% 1085.60% Gross profit $1,900,000 $3,560,000 $9,200,000 Gross profit margin 26.32% 17.31% 42.87% Extrapolating sales for the first quarter of 2019 across the year would see MedMen likely realize a minimum revenue of $85,840,000 for the financial year 2019. This puts the company's 1-year forward price-to-sales at 17. This is reasonable for a company experiencing year-on-year growth north of 1000%.
MedMen is aiming to open 66 stores by the end of 2019/2020 and has targeted store economics of $20 million per store with 50% of stocked products from [statemade] MedMen's brand.
Assuming the company is able to achieve 77% its per store target revenue and has opened 66 stores by the end of 2020, MedMen will likely see revenue of $1.016 billion by the end of the 2020 financial year. This puts the forward 2-year price-to-sales ratio to 1.4. Hence, if MedMen underperforms its own per store revenue target, the company would still trade on an incredibly low price-to-sales ratio.
November 27 post on MedMen's Instagram
The Controversy And Dilution Risk MedMen has been cloaked in controversy even before its IPO. Some of these are somewhat warranted, but some are vapid. The easiest to dismiss critique has focused on a brick-and-mortar retail rollout strategy versus an online marketplace. There is no barrier to doing both when the appropriate regulations for a comprehensive online platform for cannabis and its subsequent delivery infrastructure are in place. Further, omnichannel retailing is clearly the future of commerce as seen with Amazon's (NASDAQ: AMZN ) acquisition of Whole Foods Markets and its Amazon Go stores.
There has also been a lot of noise surrounding its executive pay and compensation structure. And it is encouraging that the company took some steps to address this. However, some very misguided commentary has also tried to depict a greedy management team that is consciously fleecing shareholders after failing to run the company in a proper manner. Fundamentally, at MedMen's current pace of growth, executive compensation will largely be immaterial in less than 3 years as executive pay and a percentage of revenue will be minuscule.
MedMen does face risk from the illegal federal status of cannabis in the US. This prohibits cannabis from being transported across state lines, essentially necessitating the construction of production facilities in every US state it expands into. And while this presents a bottleneck to achieving economies of scale in the medium term, the long-term risk from this is more subsided. Some years from now, the federal status of cannabis will likely have changed to reflect an industry employing tens of thousands of Americans and contributing hundreds of millions of dollars in tax revenue. Hence, the narrative has to change to asking whether MedMen is achieving economies of scale within the current constraints of the regulatory environment it operates in. The company using the blueprint of Mustang, its Nevada production facility, to construct of other facilities provide an example, albeit a small one, of this being the case.
MedMen's biggest risk factor comes from its multiple cash raising events which have come from consecutive quarterly losses for the company. The destructive effect of shareholder dilution has weighed heavily on the company, with shares now trading at $3.11, down almost 55% from its peak of $6.90 from October.
MMNFF data by YCharts
The cash loss has been a result of the company's hyper-aggressive expansion strategy which should pay off in the long term. MedMen is perfectly within its capacity to make a switch to profitability by putting the brakes on expansion, culling its marketing team, or reducing the scope of its internal product developments. However, doing any of these would misalign the company from its longer-term trajectory to greatness.
MedMen store on Paradise Road, Las Vegas
A Future That Could Blaze Above All Investors in MedMen face substantial risk from the company's growth strategy. This has already seen current shareholders realize a substantial dilution of their holdings. I hold little hope that this will stop in the short and potentially medium term. But dilution can be looked at from two lenses and, in some ways, rationalized. If a 2x increase in share count leads to a 4x increase in revenue and greatly increases the potential for future profit, then shareholders will not be entirely worse off.
Against this specter of dilution does stand an actual company. The fastest growing public cannabis company on Earth. A company ramping revenue and expanding rapidly in the largest and most important cannabis markets in the world while building a strong upmarket cannabis brand. MedMen presents potential investors with two stark potential outcomes with no middle ground. It will either capitulate from its expansion and collapse to nothing, or it will ascend to a tier of companies characterized by outsized profit margins and a strong return on capital employed, greatness. I am making a hard play on the latter.
Disclosure: I am/we are long MMNFF. I wrote this article myself, and it expresses my own opinions. I am not receiving compensation for it (other than from Seeking Alpha). I have no business relationship with any company whose stock is mentioned in this article.
